lectures.title: Requiring the Auth Token on the Backend

cues.en: So we implemented all that user authentication logic,
the one thing we haven't done yet is we're not protecting our back-end, we're not really using that token
other than for finding out whether we're authenticated or not.
In reality, you would have routes on your back-end that simply don't work
if you are not authenticated and we can simulate this here
too. Back on Firebase, on the database tab,
if you go to rules, you can enforce that the user needs to be authenticated by setting auth not equal
to null here for both read and write,
you're ensuring that only users where the authentication state and auth is an internal variable managed
by Firebase, so only where the authentication set is not null are allowed to read and write and this
will be set to true or to a valid value by Firebase automatically when you do pass a valid auth
token along with the request.
So we'll have to use our token to also append it to requests that reach our back-end, the same for storing
data
if we upload an image. There on storage, we also have a rules tab and we can change the rules here to
make sure that users have to be authenticated. For this instead of saying this
if true, you should check whether request which is an object passed in or provided by a Firebase auth
is unequal to null,
so same logic as in the database case in the end and now only users who added a token are allowed to
upload data. For that,
we also now need to change our cloud function a little bit because that is the thing which in the end
interacts with our back-end and with the storage and there, we now need to add logic to extract that token.
For this, we'll add a new import up there, fbAdmin which requires the Firebase admin package which already
was added to package.json before. Then here after storage where we define that storage constant, you
call fbAdmin, initialize app and pass an object to it where you have to set a credential
and now that's important,
you need to create that credential or a credentials file in your project settings, here in your Firebase
web console under
service accounts Firebase admin SDK here,
once this loaded, you leave NodeJS checked and you generate a new private key here
which gives you a downloadable file and you should download that and store that in your cloud functions
file and you can rename it to whatever you want, I'll name it ionic-app.json but you can name this file
whatever you want.
Now back in your cloud function code here in the project, you set credential equal to fbAdmin credential
cert and then you require a pointer at this file,
so in my case, a relative path pointing at ionic-app.json and this basically imports that
key for you and sets up that Firebase admin package.
Now what do we need this package for?
We'll need it for using that token later and for authenticating ourselves. Now
first of all inside of our function code here though, after checking the request method, I'll check whether
a token was added and for this, we check if specific headers were set,
if an authorization header exists or in this case if it does not exist because I want to block this function
from executing then or if it does exist, this authorization header but it does not start with bearer
which it should because we'll store the token on such a bearer
key. If either of these two things is true, then we know we'll have no token and therefore I'll return
a response with the status of 401,
with some JSON data where I set an error of unauthorized and this is now all NodeJS code, of course
attached you also find that finished function where you only need to change your credential file name
and your project name.
So we'll write it together here though, I'm checking whether such token was added to the request, if
it was added, I'll retrieve it here
by setting idToken equal to request headers authorization,
splitting this on that bearer identifier and then taking the second value which will be the actual token,
the first value would be that bearer identifier string here.
With that token extracted, we can continue down to that finish handler
and there,
I will now return a call to fbAdmin using that Firebase admin package auth, where I verify the token,
the idToken we just extracted and if that is valid, then we actually would get the decoded token here
and now all the logic we had in there before
up to this point where we have the first then block goes into here
and we add our then block thereafter.
So now we basically just start by verifying the token,
then we get the token, we know yes we are authenticated and then we simply upload the image as before
and we proceed as before,
that has not changed,
so we simply added this extra check here and the rest of the function can stay the way it is. Now after
this change,
you should run Firebase deploy again after saving this file to upload this new Firebase function
and now both the cloud function as well as our normal database require a token to be added to the requests
to successfully do their job and
that will be what we do in the next lectures.
